clippings.speaker: Dante Spinotti
clippings.quote: When I work with Michael Mann, Michael is usually very keen on his camera angles. Very rarely, if I step in, was I consulted about where or what kind of lens to use in how to do a shot. Sometimes, it happens.
clippings.title: Dante Spinotti on Michael Mann’s Preparedness, Remastering Classics, and New Technologies
clippings.context: Interviewed at Camerimage, Spinotti describes how the division of labor works on a Mann set.

clippings.speaker: Dante Spinotti
clippings.quote: I know Michael very well. We are friends and have been friends for a long, long time. Michael is, for sure, the kind of director who, if you agree with him and understand what he has in mind to do, you can work with him. If you are someone who discusses or does disagree, you better not do that.
clippings.title: Dante Spinotti on Michael Mann’s Preparedness, Remastering Classics, and New Technologies
clippings.context: Asked about Mann's famous sense of control, Spinotti describes their friendship and how to work with him.

clippings.speaker: Dante Spinotti
clippings.quote: I always found, even when I did my first movie with Michael… the way I describe it is that, for me, coming from Italy and some good television, he was like finding a way of making movies that maybe I dreamed of, in my mind, but that I actually never worked on. … He was great, and I have always highly admired him; I learned a lot from Michael Mann.
clippings.title: Dante Spinotti on Michael Mann’s Preparedness, Remastering Classics, and New Technologies
clippings.context: Spinotti recalls arriving from Italy to shoot Manhunter, his first film with Mann.

clippings.speaker: Dante Spinotti
clippings.quote: At some point, Michael turned to me and said, “Dante, why did you turn this up in the forest?” I said, “Michael, that is the sun.” He hadn’t realized that the sun was up!
clippings.title: Dante Spinotti on Michael Mann’s Preparedness, Remastering Classics, and New Technologies
clippings.context: Spinotti's anecdote about dimming tungsten lights up with the dawn during a night exterior with Magua.

clippings.speaker: Dante Spinotti
clippings.quote: I think the allure for Michael Mann, and obviously for myself, was to be able to shoot this period film in a very modern, agile, aggressive and, I think, dynamic camera style.
clippings.title: Michael Mann Takes a Shot in the Dark With Public Enemies
clippings.context: Spinotti on why he and Mann shot their 1930s gangster film on Sony F23 digital cameras.

clippings.speaker: Michael Mann
clippings.quote: If people are as ambitious as you are, you keep them close to you. … Cinematographer Dante Spinotti and I have done five movies together.
clippings.title: The Study of Mann
clippings.context: Asked by F.X. Feeney how he assembles his recurring team, Mann names Spinotti among his longtime collaborators.

notes: Mann rarely speaks about Spinotti in print; only the DGA mention found (HCA tribute and Manhunter Q&A are video-only, Locarno pages are JS-rendered). Spinotti's Mohicans excerpt on michael-mann.blogspot.com skipped because its original source was unclear.
